description: Permanently delete the signed-in person's account — profile, friendships, messages and requests. There is no undo on the server.
Everything Towinly holds about the signed-in person, in one object, as GET /account/export returns it. Nothing is emailed; the caller decides how the copy reaches the person (download, share sheet).

Ask the Towinly assistant one question, with the recent turns for context. Waits up to 30s, not the client default 15s: a thoughtful Groq answer can outrun 15s under load, and a timeout reads as "the AI is broken" (owner report from the first TestFlight build, 2026-08-17).

children.name: message
children.text: the question, already trimmed and non-empty

description: Ask for a password-reset email. The backend answers the same whether or not the address has an account, so a resolved call never proves one exists.
Set a new password using the token from the emailed reset link.

children.name: token
children.text: the reset token off the link's query string

description: Send the signed-in account's email-verification link again. Used from the verify-pending gate when the first email never arrived.
Start a Towinly signup. No account exists until the person opens the emailed link, so this never returns a session — the caller sends them to check their inbox.
Send the confirmation email again for a signup that has not been opened yet. No account exists at this point, so nobody is logged in when this runs.
Confirm an emailed signup link. This is what actually creates the account: the backend checks the token and finishes the signup it belongs to.
Set the first password on a Google-signup account that has none yet (profile hasPassword === false). No current password exists, so none is sent. Signing in with Google keeps working afterwards.
Change the signed-in account's password. The backend checks the current one before accepting the new one.
The people the signed-in account has blocked, newest first.
Block one person. Idempotent on the server: blocking twice is one block.
Unblock one person. Never an error when they were not blocked.

Every connection the signed-in person is part of — friendships and family links alike — with status, current trust level, per-side confirm flags, and the other person's id and name, as GET /connections returns it.

Elders near the signed-in helper who could use company, closest first, as GET /discover/elders returns them. The distance goes on the wire — without it the backend caps the search at its own 10 km default.

description: Helpers near the signed-in elder, closest first, as GET /discover/helpers returns them. The distance goes on the wire — without it the backend caps the search at its own 10 km default.

params.text: how far to look, in kilometres

children.text: true to let family see it, false to keep it private

description: The signed-in account's emergency contacts (at most 3).

params.type: {name: string, phone: string, relationship: string, inactivityDays: number|string}
params.name: contact

description: Remove one emergency contact by its id.
Send an SOS: immediately alert every one of the signed-in person's emergency contacts that they need help.
Which of the signed-in elder's family members are connected with which helpers — Step 4 transparency: nothing about you happens out of your sight. Names and ids only, never contact details.
The signed-in person's family links from both seats, as GET /family/links returns them: activeLinks (each saying whether I am the elder in it) and any pending invitations.

Who stands behind each of the signed-in helper's elder friendships — the family members those elders have chosen to share with, as GET /family/behind-me returns them (an `entries` array keyed by connectionId). Derived server-side from the elder's own sharing.
The family member's view of each linked parent's journey: check-in, open requests, and the friendships the parent chose to share, as GET /family/journey returns it (an object with `elders`).
The alerts a family member sees about their linked parents (SOS, quiet lately, new friendships), newest first. In-app only — nothing is sent by text or email.
Ask to link with someone as family. Nothing is shared until they accept.

children.text: what the identified person is (Daughter, Son, …)

children.text: the seat the IDENTIFIED person takes: 'elder' = adding your parent, 'family' = an elder adding a family member

description: Answer a pending family link request. Accepting turns the link ACTIVE; declining removes it.

children.name: accept

description: The elder answers a family member's ask for a delegated power (acting for them). A yes grants exactly that one power; a no changes nothing.

children.name: accept

description: Remove a family link — an active member, or a request still waiting. The other person loses all sight of the elder; either seat can call it.

description: Make one active family member the elder's main contact — the person the app names first when something needs family attention.

Remove the family member's inherited standing on one shared friendship. Reversible: resumeFamilyStanding restores the same connection.
Open (or reopen) the direct chat an inherited standing allows with the elder's helper — no request, no accept.

The one-page copy the server builds from her box list — names only, no decrypted bodies — plus when she last saved a copy.
